q: For a Group I project with a PCC over P1.0 billion, what is the base fee amount before adding the percentage of excess, under the DADS schedule?
n: Under the Group I DADS schedule, a PCC over P1.0 billion is billed at P11,100,000 plus 0.6% of the excess over P1.0 billion. P18,500,000 and P13,500,000 are DAEDS base figures, and P8,100,000 is the DADS base for the 500M-1B bracket.

q: Using the Group I DAEDS schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: DAEDS formula: P2,500,000 + 4% of excess over P50M.
scenario: A warehouse (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P80,000,000.00, which falls in the "over P50.0 million to P100.0 million" bracket.
formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

q: Using the Group I DADS schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: DADS formula: P2,700,000 + 1.8% of excess over P100M.
scenario: An industrial building (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P175,000,000.00, which falls in the "over P100.0 million to P200.0 million" bracket.
formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

q: An architect is engaged to design a public market (a Group I building). The Owner wants the Architect to be the sole point of contract responsibility, with the structural, electrical, and sanitary engineers each entering into sub-consultancy agreements with the Architect rather than contracting directly with the Owner. Which mode of engagement is this?
n: A single Architect-Owner contract, with the Architect sub-contracting the engineering/allied professionals, describes DAEDS (Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services).

n: At exactly P50.0 million, the PCC falls in the "P50.0 million and less" bracket, billed at 3% of PCC: 3% x P50,000,000 = P1,500,000.00, matching the base figure of the next DADS bracket (P1,500,000 + 2.4% of excess).
scenario: A public market (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of exactly P50,000,000.00.
formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

scenario: A simple loft-type building (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P30,000,000.00, which falls in the "P50.0 million and less" bracket.

q: Under both the DAEDS and DADS modes of engagement, what happens to the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional involved?
o: They are automatically merged and assumed solely by the Architect as Lead Professional
They are shared equally regardless of who performed the work
They are transferred entirely to the Owner
They stay separate; the Architect does not assume the others' liabilities
n: Sec. 6.1 states that in both DAEDS and DADS, the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate; the Architect does not assume any of the responsibilities and liabilities of the other RLPs.

q: Under SPP Document 202's grouping of buildings for Regular Design Services, what best characterizes Building Type Group I?
o: Buildings of the simplest utilization and character, without complication of plan/design or detail, requiring only a minimum of architectural finishes, engineering, and allied architectural elements
Buildings requiring extensive and highly complex detailing beyond ordinary practice
Buildings of moderate complexity of plan/design requiring a moderate amount of research and of engineering and allied architectural design
Buildings of exceptional character and complexity of plan/design requiring comparatively large amounts of research and of engineering and allied architectural design
n: Sec. 6.3.1 defines Group I as buildings of the simplest utilization and character, without complication of plan/design or detail, requiring only a minimum of architectural finishes, engineering, and allied architectural elements. (b) describes Group II and (c) describes Group III.

q: How much MORE would the Owner pay in RPF under DAEDS compared to DADS for this project?
n: DAEDS RPF at PCC=P175M is P6,750,000.00 (P4,500,000 + 3% of P75M excess) and DADS RPF is P4,050,000.00 (P2,700,000 + 1.8% of P75M excess). Difference = P6,750,000 - P4,050,000 = P2,700,000.00, reflecting the added sub-consultancy administration scope the Architect carries under DAEDS.
scenario: An architect is comparing the total Recommended Professional Fee an Owner would pay for the same Group I hangar project (PCC = P175,000,000.00) under DAEDS versus under DADS.
steps: DAEDS RPF at PCC=P175M is P6,750,000.00 (P4,500,000 + 3% of P75M excess) and DADS RPF is P4,050,000.00 (P2,700,000 + 1.8% of P75M excess)
Difference = P6,750,000 - P4,050,000 = P2,700,000.00, reflecting the added sub-consultancy administration scope the Architect carries under DAEDS

n: Sec. 6.3.1 lists Habitable Agricultural Buildings, Hangars, Industrial Buildings, and Manufacturing/Industrial Plants together as Group I building types.

q: Which of the following building types is explicitly listed under Group I (Simple) in SPP Document 202?
n: Warehouses are listed under Group I. Hospitals/Medical Buildings are Group III (exceptional complexity); Schools and Shopping Centers are Group II (moderate complexity).

q: Which of the following is listed as a Group I building type under SPP Document 202?
n: Public Markets fall under Group I. Banks/Financial Institutions and Residential Condominiums are Group II buildings, while Convention Facilities belong to Group III.

q: A developer building a warehouse (Group I) wants each of the structural and electrical engineers to sign their own direct contracts with the company, separate from the Architect's contract. Which mode of engagement should the Architect use to properly bill Recommended Professional Fees for this arrangement?
n: When the Architect and the engineering/allied professionals each execute separate, direct contracts with the Owner, this is DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services), which uses its own lower RPF bracket schedule since the Architect no longer administers sub-consultancy contracts.

q: For a Group I project with a PCC between P100.0 million and P200.0 million, what is the correct DADS fee formula?
o: P4,500,000 plus 1.2% of the excess over P200.0 million
P2,500,000 plus 4% of the excess over P50.0 million
P2,700,000 plus 1.8% of the excess over P100.0 million
P4,500,000 plus 3% of the excess over P100.0 million
n: The Group I DADS bracket for PCC over P100.0 million up to P200.0 million is P2,700,000 plus 1.8% of the excess over P100.0 million. P4,500,000 plus 3% of the excess over P100.0 million is the DAEDS formula for the same bracket.

q: Aside from the enumerated building types, Sec. 6.3.1 of SPP Document 202 extends the Group I classification to which category?
o: Any building under 50 million pesos regardless of use
n: The Group I list ends with a catch-all clause, "Other similar utilization type buildings," extending the classification to comparable simple-use structures not individually named.

q: SPP Document 202's building type groupings (Group I through Group X) primarily exist to accomplish what purpose?
o: To set minimum floor area requirements for each building type
To set fair remuneration by the complexity and skill the work needs
To assign projects exclusively to either DAEDS or DADS with no other basis for choice
To determine which projects require a building permit
n: Sec. 6.2 explains that professional architectural work is classified according to the degree of complexity and creative skill required to meet the Client's requirements, and this grouping of buildings is provided to determine fair remuneration for the Architect.

q: In DAEDS, how does the Architect contractually relate to the engineering and allied professionals working on the project?
o: The Architect has no contractual relationship with them at all
Through sub-consultancy contracts between the Architect and the other professionals
The other professionals contract directly and separately with the Owner
The Owner subcontracts the other professionals to the general contractor
n: Under DAEDS, there is a single contract between the Architect and the Owner, and the Architect enters into sub-consultancy contracts with the other professionals working with the Architect.

q: Using the Group I DAEDS schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: DAEDS formula: P13,500,000 + 1% of excess over P500M.
scenario: A packaging and processing plant (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P750,000,000.00, which falls in the "over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion" bracket.
formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

q: For Group I buildings, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for DAEDS when the Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P50.0 million or less?
n: Per the Group I DAEDS bracket schedule, a PCC of P50.0 million and less carries an RPF of 5% of PCC.

q: An architect is asked which of the following does NOT belong to Building Type Group I. Which one should the architect identify as the odd one out?
n: Hotels are classified under Group III (buildings of exceptional character and complexity), not Group I. Service Garages, Bakeries, and Parking Structures are all listed under Group I.

q: Using the Group I DADS schedule, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF)?
n: DADS formula: P8,100,000 + 0.6% of excess over P500M.
scenario: A packaging and processing plant (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P750,000,000.00, which falls in the "over P500.0 million to P1.0 billion" bracket.
formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

q: SPP Document 202's Group I schedule is found under which section, covering "Regular Design Services"?
n: The Group I building type classification and its RPF bracket schedules appear under Sec. 6, "Regular Design Services," of SPP Document 202.

q: Under SPP Document 202, what does "DADS" stand for?
n: DADS stands for Detailed Architectural Design Services, where the Architect and the engineering/allied professionals each execute separate, direct contracts with the Owner.

q: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.2 lists several methods by which the Architect's compensation for Regular Design Services may be based. Which of the following is one of those listed methods?
o: Percentage of the Owner's annual gross revenue
n: Sec. 6.2.1 lists Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost (PCC) as one of the recognized methods of compensation, alongside Unit Cost Method, Professional Fee plus Expenses, Lump Sum/Fixed Fee, Per Diem/Honorarium plus Reimbursable Expenses, Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses, and Mixed Methods.

q: Comparing the Group I RPF schedules, why is the DAEDS percentage/fee consistently higher than the DADS fee at every matching PCC bracket?
o: The Architect also runs the sub-consultancy contracts and coordination
Because DADS is only used for renovation work while DAEDS is only for new construction
Because the percentages are arbitrary and unrelated to scope
Because DAEDS always covers a larger physical floor area than DADS
n: DAEDS involves a single Architect-Owner contract under which the Architect also enters sub-consultancy contracts with the engineering/allied professionals, adding coordination and administrative scope beyond DADS (where those professionals contract directly with the Owner) — which is reflected in the consistently higher DAEDS percentages/fees.

q: For Group I buildings, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for DADS when the Project Construction Cost (PCC) is P50.0 million or less?
n: Per the Group I DADS bracket schedule, a PCC of P50.0 million and less carries an RPF of 3% of PCC (lower than the corresponding DAEDS rate of 5% since DADS excludes the Architect's sub-consultancy administration of the other professionals).

q: Under SPP Document 202, what does "DAEDS" stand for as one of the two ways the Architect may provide Regular Design Services?
o: Detailed Architectural Estimate and Design Services
Design, Architectural, Engineering, and Documentation Services
Direct Architectural and Engineering Delivery System
Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services
n: DAEDS stands for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services: a single contract between the Architect and the Owner, with the Architect entering sub-consultancy contracts with the other professionals.

scenario: A warehouse (a Group I building under SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3.1) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of P80,000,000.00, which falls in the "over P50.0 million to P100.0 million" bracket.
formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

q: Printing plants and packaging/processing plants are classified under which building type group?
n: Printing Plants and Packaging and Processing Plants are both expressly enumerated as Group I (Simple) buildings in Sec. 6.3.1.

q: A client asks an architect whether a proposed service garage with straightforward finishes and no unusual architectural detailing should be billed using the Group I or a higher group's fee schedule. Based on SPP Document 202, how should the architect respond?
o: Group I, since service garages are enumerated under Group I as simple buildings requiring only minimum finishes and engineering elements
Group II, since garages always require moderate architectural research
Group III, since any building involving vehicles is automatically classified as exceptional
It cannot be classified under any group without a court ruling
n: Service Garages are explicitly listed as a Group I building type in Sec. 6.3.1, so a straightforward service garage with minimal finishes is correctly billed under the Group I RPF schedule.

formula: RPF = base of bracket + rate × (PCC − lower limit of bracket)

q: The Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) bracket schedules for Group I (by DAEDS and DADS case) found in Sec. 6.3.1 are computed as which method of compensation under Sec. 6.2?
o: Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses
n: The Group I RPF tables express the Architect's fee as a percentage of Project Construction Cost (PCC), which is method 6.2.1, Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost.

q: An architect is hired to design a simple loft-type building. During construction, the structural engineer (a separate RLP hired directly by the Owner under a DADS arrangement) makes a design error that causes a structural defect. Under SPP Document 202, who bears the professional responsibility and civil liability for that error?
o: The Architect, since the Architect is the Lead Professional and automatically assumes all liabilities
The structural engineer, since responsibilities and liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate regardless of DAEDS or DADS
No one, since SPP Document 202 does not address liability
The Owner, since the Owner selected the engineer
n: Sec. 6.1 is explicit that in both DAEDS and DADS, liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate; the Architect does not assume the responsibilities and liabilities of the other RLPs — here, the structural engineer bears responsibility for the structural design error.

q: For a Group I project with a PCC between P50.0 million and P100.0 million, what is the correct DAEDS fee formula?
o: P4,500,000 plus 3% of the excess over P100.0 million
P2,500,000 plus 4% of the excess over P50.0 million
P1,500,000 plus 2.4% of the excess over P50.0 million
P3,000,000 plus 5% of the excess over P50.0 million
n: The Group I DAEDS bracket for PCC over P50.0 million up to P100.0 million is P2,500,000 plus 4% of the excess over P50.0 million. P1,500,000 plus 2.4% is the DADS formula for the same bracket, and P4,500,000 plus 3% is the next DAEDS bracket.
